overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the evidence of a quorum deliberation outside a meeting was contradictory and insufficient. It declined to review the minutes and jurisdiction allegations, and only issued a reminder.

allegations.summary: A complainant alleged that a quorum of the Planning Board discussed her proposed bed and breakfast outside a noticed meeting, before a July 2017 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The versions of events provided by the four Board members are contradictory, and we cannot arrive at a formal finding of what conversation, if any, occurred.

allegations.summary: A supplementary complaint alleged that the July 13, 2017 meeting minutes contained inaccuracies. This was raised for the first time after the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: Because these allegations were not part of the complaint filed with the Board, we decline to review them.

allegations.summary: The complainant argued that the Board's decision to initiate site plan review was outside its purview.
allegations.key_passage: we note that this allegation, even if true, would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
